reviewer.agent: Claude Code (file handoff; environment names the handoff channel)

themes.label: Hosting UNESCO AI research centre
themes.definition: Promotion of a nationally hosted, UNESCO-backed international AI research centre focused on AI governance and policy.
themes.inclusion: Include passages proposing, seeking support for or announcing the launch of an international AI centre under UNESCO auspices.
themes.exclusion: Exclude calls for UN governance bodies not tied to a hosted centre.
themes.boundary_cases: This is both a national initiative and a UN-system contribution; code AI_UN_ROLE additionally if broader UN processes are discussed.

examples.quote: the very first UNESCO global center for artificial intelligence established in Ljubljana last November
The aim of the centre will be to provide an open environment, focusing on the governance and policies surrounding artificial intelligence.
the International Research Centre on Artificial Intelligence, in Ljubljana, the capital of Slovenia, in March 2021

themes.label: Algocracy and regulating AI for rights
themes.definition: Concern about 'algocracy' and the need to regulate AI's impact on human rights and frame technology in service of humankind.
themes.inclusion: Include passages on regulating AI's human rights impact or ensuring technology serves humankind.
themes.boundary_cases: 'Frame them in service of humankind' counts here when referring to AI.

examples.quote: We need to be better prepared for the challenge of algocracy, including by regulating the impact of artificial intelligence on human rights protection.

themes.label: AI transforming work and daily life
themes.definition: AI described as transforming work, productivity and daily life, and as the backbone of business and public services.
themes.inclusion: Include passages on AI's role in future work, productivity, or as infrastructure of daily economic life.
themes.boundary_cases: Statements that AI is part of daily life without economic content may be AI_TECH_LIST_MENTION.

examples.quote: According to estimates, as much as 80 per cent of future work will be done using artificial intelligence.
New technologies and artificial intelligence have already become the backbone of our daily lives that keep businesses and essential public services running.

themes.label: Emerging technologies for climate and agriculture
themes.definition: Responsible use of new technologies to address climate change, agriculture, mobility and education.
themes.inclusion: Include passages listing AI/new technology applications for development and sustainability.
themes.boundary_cases: Where AI is implied only through 'new technologies', code if the passage links to an AI initiative.

examples.quote: New technologies offer numerous opportunities to mitigate climate change, support sustainable agriculture, introduce smarter mobility, offer better education

value.rationale: Slovenian passages (2019-2021) center on promoting the UNESCO-backed AI research centre in Ljubljana, framed by rights concerns (algocracy), AI's transformation of work and daily life, and its development applications.
